key_insight: A lone-pair-rich hybrid perovskite, GuaPbI3, achieves ultralow thermal conductivity because chemically induced lattice softness suppresses phonon transport while preserving accessible electronic states.
engineering_relevance: This design principle points to a new route for thermoelectric and thermal-management materials: engineer soft, electronically heterogeneous lattices to decouple low heat flow from usable charge transport.
method: Physics-guided symbolic regression screened for lone-pair-dominated compositions with low lattice thermal conductivity.
Mechanochemical synthesis produced crystalline GuaPbI3 for experimental validation.
Electrical, impedance, and DFT analyses probed bulk transport, band structure, and lattice-electron coupling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.088 W m^-1 K^-1, with bulk-dominated transport and bias-dependent conduction confirmed by electrical and impedance measurements.
watch_item: Charge transport appears sensitive to chemical potential and morphology-independent performance may still be challenging to translate into stable, device-ready architectures.
paper_title: Lone-Pair-Induced Lattice Softness Enables Ultralow Thermal Conductivity in Hybrid Organic-Inorganic Perovskite GuaPbI$_3$
